title: Feudal pyramid sheet
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Medieval peasants and the Black Death (Peasants, Princes & Pestilence)
source: Written for history/y5 lesson 17 (Feudal pyramid sheet (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 17: The feudal system. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Land for loyalty
points: The king owned all the land
He gave land in return for service

panels.title: Why it worked
points: Breaking a promise lost your land
The king could raise an army

parts.text: Who: a trained soldier on horseback
Got: a manor with land and peasants
So: he stayed loyal to keep his land

keywords.def: land given in return for loyalty and service
a powerful lord given land by the king

questions.q: What did a peasant get in return for work?
questions.a: A strip of land and protection

questions.q: Who was at the top of the feudal system?
What did knights give their baron?
Core: Draw and label the feudal pyramid, writing what each level gave and received.
questions.a: A four-level pyramid with accurate gave and received labels

questions.q: Extend: Write a paragraph: was the feudal system fair to peasants? Give a reason.
questions.a: Not very fair: peasants worked hardest for the least, though they had protection

questions.q: Stretch: Why might a baron break his promise to a king?
questions.a: If the king was weak or unfair, a baron might want more power

questions.q: Most people in medieval England were:
questions.a: C) Peasants. Peasants were by far the largest group, at the bottom of the pyramid.

questions.q: The feudal system swapped land for:
Big question: why would a knight fight for a baron?
questions.a: To keep the land the baron gave him in return for service
